title: Taganrog Fortress

terrainReference.basis: Reference from independent terrain source near the central street blocks of the former fortress. Modern terrain approximates general slope and known cape grade.

mapIdentity.provider: Russian State Archive of Ancient Acts 1704 survey, historical bastion site and current OpenStreetMap coastline
mapIdentity.scope: Engineering sheet RGADA fond 9, inventory 2, file 66, no. 34 shows the named cape, four fronts, three bastions, two half bastions, four ravelins, and the stone moles. The contour, directions and relative sizes follow the survey with its compass and scale. The third-bastion commemoration at Petrovskaya 15 constrains approximate geographic registration.

note: The original sectional drawings show tiered earth, dry ditch, a central drain, covered way and glacis. Construction remains in progress in 1704. The later Qualla Lyall plate is a cross-check for the tip of the cape and harbor geometry. It depicts the early nineteenth-century town.
